summary: Agent implemented the checkbox directly in index.html within ~15s, with no brainstorming skill invocation and no clarifying questions.
reasoning: The request was handled mechanically: one Read, a directory listing, one bash call, then a single Edit inserting a native checkbox. No Skill tool invocation appears anywhere in the session log, and the agent explicitly declined to brainstorm. Both acceptance criteria pass.

observations.description: The agent's first user-visible line is jargon leaking internal process: 'Rung 2 on the ladder — a basic form control with one obvious implementation, so no brainstorming needed.' A developer who asked for a checkbox has no idea what 'Rung 2 on the ladder' means.

coding-agent-token-usage.json (the headline artifact this scenario measures) was not present in the results directory at the time of my check; only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json existed. It presumably gets written after the run, but I could not observe the token total.
Skill names in the loaded plugin are 'hyperpowers:brainstorming', while the story/acceptance criteria refer to 'superpowers:brainstorming'. Naming mismatch could confuse evaluation.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Read 1 file, listed 1 directory, ran 1 shell command' then 'Rung 2 on the ladder — a basic form control with one obvious implementation, so no brainstorming needed.' followed immediately by Update(index.html) adding '<input type="checkbox"> Done'. File on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains '<input type="checkbox"> Done'. No clarifying questions were asked. 'Churned for 15s'.

grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' over the session jsonl returned only: 2 Bash, 1 Edit, 1 Read — no Skill tool call. The only 'brainstorming' hits in the log are the system-prompt skill-rule text, the skill name list ('skillCount':27, names include hyperpowers:brainstorming), and the assistant's text 'so no brainstorming needed.'
